key_insight: MeanFlowNFT adapts forward-process RL to MeanFlow by converting average-velocity sampling into an induced instantaneous-velocity objective, enabling reward alignment without sacrificing few-step generation speed.
engineering_relevance: This makes fast generative models easier to optimize for human preferences or downstream tasks while keeping inference cheap and practical for image/video deployment.
method: Construct an induced instantaneous-velocity predictor from the MeanFlow identity.
Apply the DiffusionNFT forward-process RL objective to that predictor.
Keep sampling with the original average velocity to preserve fast few-step generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains on image and video benchmarks, including outperforming prior RL-tuned few-step generators on 6 of 8 metrics on SD3.5-M and a 4-step Wan 2.1 model reaching VBench 84.33 versus 82.57 for a 50-step baseline.
watch_item: The approach depends on a correct induced-velocity formulation and stable reward optimization, so implementation errors or reward misalignment could reduce the expected policy-improvement benefit.
paper_title: MeanFlowNFT: Bringing Forward-Process RL to Average-Velocity Generators
